messages.subject: fMRI model regressors
parts:
Hi 

Thank you for this fantastic and very timely software.

Would you be able to let me know how far into the future extraction of fMRI model regressors might be implemented into the package? I am interested in the IGT, potentially. Is there a workaround in the meantime? Also, is there a way to covary IQ in this task?

Thanks again for excellent work!

Luke.

messages.author: 47d1400f432367d7
messages.subject: Re: fMRI model regressors
parts:
Hi Luke,


For extracting fMRI model regressors—this is something we would like to do soon, but I am unsure on the exact timeline. In the mean-time, you may want to take a look at the .stan code for the go/nogo models (i.e. gng_*.stan). Those models already work, and if you feel comfortable modifying the IGT .stan code to extract the relevant information, it should work just fine.  


For covarying values with external data, the package will not do this automatically right now, but it should be something that could be done in the .stan codes with some modification. For example, if the learning rate is assumed to covary with IQ, then you could make each subjects' individual-level learning rate (A) a linear model of some base learning rate (e.g. A0) and the effect of IQ on the learning rate (e.g. A1). Then, each subjects' learning rate would be: 


A[i] = A0[i] + A1[i] * IQ[i]


where i indexes the subject number. If the group-level distribution over the effect of IQ (mu_A1) ends up being no different than 0, then the inference would be that IQ does not influence learning rate (at least not assuming a linear relationship). I should note that there are many other ways to do this, but this is the first that came to mind. 


Best,

Nate
